## Laguna Hedionda: an optional stop on a route across the Altiplano

[Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) is a high-altitude lake in southwestern Bolivia. Dry Andean slopes frame its shores, while flamingos can be found in the shallow water. The name is sometimes rendered in Russian as Edionda or Edyónda: these are alternative names for the same geographical feature, not different lakes.

The lagoon lies along routes through the Lipez region toward the Siloli Desert. Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which a visit to the lagoon is **optional**. For travelers whose main itinerary focuses on the Uyuni Salt Flats and other regions, it is an opportunity to spend a separate day among saline high-altitude lakes.

## Where Hedionda appears as an optional excursion

The [18-day VIP journey through Peru, the Amazon and Bolivia](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/) offers a separate optional route through the Altiplano lagoons. It mentions Laguna Colorada, Canapa, Hedionda, Chiar Khota and Honda, as well as Ollagüe Volcano and the Chiguana Salt Flat.

This is not an ordinary short excursion from Uyuni. Travel along high-altitude roads takes considerable time, and stops depend on road conditions and overall logistics. The basic VIP tour already includes the Uyuni Salt Flats and Incahuasi Island, but **the separate day via Hedionda must be arranged in advance**, including the cost of transport, meals and accommodation if required.

For travelers primarily interested in the lagoons, we offer a [3-day jeep tour of the salt flats and southwestern Bolivia](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/). Its main itinerary visits Hedionda together with [Laguna Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/) and Canapa on the way between the volcanic landscapes and the Siloli Desert. Unlike an optional extension, the highlands occupy a substantial part of this trip.

## What you will see at the lake

The shores of Hedionda feature cold high-altitude scenery: shallow stretches of water, mineral deposits, sparse vegetation and open mountain views. Birds feed in the water, with vast plateaus stretching around them. Unlike [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), which draws attention for its reddish water, Hedionda offers a quieter combination of clear shallows, birds and mountains.

Allow time to observe birds from a distance. Do not approach feeding flamingos too closely. Bird concentrations vary with the season, time of day and water conditions.

Official Bolivian conservation materials link flamingo protection to the region's network of high-altitude lagoons. Traveling through these areas is especially rewarding for visitors who want to experience the flora and fauna of the high Andes, rather than only colorful scenery.

## Hedionda, Honda and Colorada: how they differ

| Lake | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) | Flamingos and shallow mountain waters |
| [Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/) | Pale shores and expansive scenery |
| [Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) | Reddish water |

These lagoons often appear together because the road crosses the same broad high-altitude region. More important than ticking off every name is allowing enough time to stop, watch birds and travel safely.

## What to consider on the high-altitude road

The Altiplano can bring strong winds, freezing mornings, intense sunshine and sudden weather changes. Routes involve long drives through remote areas. Plan drinking water, warm clothing, meals and the pace of travel with the altitude in mind. This is particularly important for people who have recently arrived from lowland areas.

When choosing an optional excursion, check how it fits with required flights from Uyuni or La Paz. A packed schedule without spare time can prevent a proper visit to the lagoons. If time is limited, it is more sensible to choose a basic Uyuni itinerary than to expect to cover the entire southern region in a few hours.

## Frequently asked questions about Laguna Hedionda

### What is Laguna Hedionda?

A high-altitude lake in the Lipez region of southwestern Bolivia, known for flamingo watching and its proximity to other Altiplano lakes.

### Can you visit it without adding a separate day?

That depends on the itinerary. It is part of the main route on the [3-day jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/). The [18-day VIP program](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/) mentions it on an optional high-altitude day.

### Are Hedionda and Edionda different places?

No. "Edionda" and "Edyonda" are alternative Russian renderings of the name Laguna Hedionda.

### Are flamingo sightings guaranteed?

No. Flamingos are wild birds whose numbers and whereabouts depend on conditions. They should be watched from a safe distance.

## Which tours pass through Laguna Hedionda?

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) on their main itineraries. It is one of the lakes of Bolivia's southwestern highlands that travelers visit by road between the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/).

**The shortest option considered here** is the [3-day jeep tour of Uyuni and the high-altitude lagoons](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/). On **day 2**, the route passes [Laguna Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/), Hedionda and [Canapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/), then continues toward the Stone Tree, Ollagüe Volcano and Puerto Chuvica. Day 3 is dedicated to the Uyuni Salt Flats, Colchani and Incahuasi Island. This option suits travelers who primarily want to see the salt flats, mineral lakes and volcanic landscapes on one jeep journey.

The longer [10-day tour through Bolivia's natural regions](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/) includes Hedionda on **day 3**. Travelers cross Lipez, visit the Joyas Altoandinas group of lagoons and spend the night in the Siloli area. Later the journey continues to the Amazon, Madidi National Park and Lake Titicaca. Here the lagoon is part of a broader exploration of one country's natural environments.

To combine Bolivia with neighboring countries, consider the [14-day itinerary through Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/). On **day 10**, travelers see Hedionda, Honda, Canapa and [Ramaditas](/bolivia/place/laguna-ramaditas/) on the drive to Ojo de Perdiz. The even longer [33-day VIP tour of Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) includes the lagoon on **day 17**, during an extensive Altiplano crossing toward the Chilean border.

| Trip format | Visit to Hedionda |
|---|---|
| 3-day jeep tour | Day 2, lagoons and Siloli |
| 10 days in Bolivia | Day 3, Joyas Altoandinas group |
| 14 days, three countries | Day 10, drive to Ojo de Perdiz |
| 33-day VIP itinerary | Day 17, crossing into Chile |

In each program, Hedionda is a **scheduled stop**, not an optional excursion that must be added separately. However, the time spent beside the water, access to the shore and the chance of seeing birds at close range cannot be guaranteed in advance. These depend on the particular drive and natural conditions.

## Why stop at Hedionda?

The lagoon lies among dry volcanic slopes and saline high-altitude lakes. Its scenery combines shallow water, pale salt deposits, mountains and open skies. Flamingos are often found in this area, feeding in the shallows where natural food is available.

The name **Hedionda** is associated with the distinctive odor that can sometimes be noticed near the lake due to sulfur compounds. Russian-language itineraries may therefore refer to it as **"Khedionda", "Edionda" or "Edyonda"**. All refer to the same place; Ada Tours records these variants in its catalog.

Bring binoculars or a camera with an optical zoom for birdwatching. Avoid approaching flamingos too closely for a photograph: a startled flock may abandon its feeding area. It is better to observe from an accessible trail and follow your guide's directions. Wildlife and bird numbers vary by season, so it would be misleading to promise "hundreds of flamingos" on every departure.

The experience differs from visiting [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), famed for the reddish tones of its water. Hedionda is particularly interesting for viewing birds against the backdrop of a mineral lake. Visiting both reveals more of the diversity of the high-altitude lakes of southwestern Bolivia.

## How the lagoon fits the route between Uyuni and Siloli

On the [3-day jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), **day 2** begins with a series of lagoons. Honda, Hedionda and Canapa come first, followed by the Stone Tree, Ollagüe Volcano and the Puerto Chuvica area. Accommodation is in a salt hotel. It is a full day of driving with several stops at lakes, rather than a separate day-long hike.

The [10-day journey](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/) follows a different route through this area: from Tahua, across the volcanic landscapes of Lipez toward the lagoons and the Siloli Desert. **Day 3** includes Canapa, Hedionda, Chiar Khota and Honda. This day includes private 4×4 transport, a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking guide, admission tickets, breakfast, lunch and dinner, and a night at Hotel Tayka del Desierto. These inclusions apply **specifically to this 10-day program**, not every tour in the catalog.

On the [14-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/), the lagoons are visited during the drive from the Uyuni area to Ojo de Perdiz. After breakfast, travelers pass Hedionda, Honda, Canapa and Ramaditas. A packed lunch and overnight accommodation are specified for this section. This option is suitable for travelers who want to connect highland Bolivia with the attractions of Peru and then continue into Chile.

## Other places to see along the same road

Other distinctive natural sites feature in current itineraries near Hedionda, each offering something different.

**[Laguna Canapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/)** is part of the same chain of lakes. It is frequently mentioned alongside Hedionda and Honda on routes across Lipez.

**[Laguna Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/)** is another stop among the mineral lakes. When choosing a busy itinerary featuring birds and several lagoons, consider the complete chain of stops rather than a single photograph in a tour description.

**[Laguna Chiar Khota](/bolivia/place/laguna-chiar-khota-potosi/)** appears on some longer trips. Whether it is visited on a given day depends on the itinerary.

**[Laguna Ramaditas](/bolivia/place/laguna-ramaditas/)** is included, in particular, on the 14- and 33-day routes across Bolivia and Chile. It should not automatically be assumed to be part of every short trip to Hedionda.

Farther on, the road leads to the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) and natural attractions around the [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). These include [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/). Think of them as further stops on a particular multi-day route: visiting Hedionda does not mean that all these sites are covered on the same day.

## How to choose the right trip

If your main goal is **Uyuni and several high-altitude lagoons**, start by comparing the 3-day jeep tour. It is a concentrated road journey through remote terrain, passing a succession of natural attractions.

If you would like to see **several different natural regions of Bolivia**, compare the 10-day tour. After the high-altitude desert, the journey continues to tropical forests and Lake Titicaca, with considerably more time devoted to the country.

If you are planning a **three-country itinerary**, pay particular attention to the border-crossing direction, overnight stops and number of days in Bolivia. The [14-day program](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) and [33-day VIP program](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) both include Hedionda, but differ in overall duration and trip arrangements. The word "VIP" in a title does not establish a particular hotel, vehicle type or private arrangement for every excursion; inclusions depend on the selected product description.

Find out in advance how much time is actually allowed for stops by the lagoons, where you will stay overnight and which stretches of the journey take place at altitude. Altiplano roads involve long drives across open terrain. Even without much physical exertion, the cold, dry air and altitude require preparation. Bring warm layers, sun protection and drinking water, and discuss acclimatization to altitude with the organizer.

For journeys focused on wildlife and birdwatching, also explore [nature-themed tours of Bolivia](/interests/wildlife/tours/bolivia/). That catalog lists relevant active itineraries, whereas this page focuses exclusively on trips that pass through Hedionda.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Laguna Hedionda and Edionda different lakes?

No. **Edionda and Edyonda** are alternative Russian renderings of the Spanish name **Hedionda**. In the Ada Tours catalog, they all refer to the same Laguna Hedionda in Bolivia.

### Can I see the lagoon on a 3-day tour?

Yes. The [3-day jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/) schedules Hedionda on **day 2**, together with Honda and Canapa. It is a stop on the road journey.

### Must I visit the Uyuni Salt Flats to see Hedionda?

There is no single required sequence for every route. The 3-day tour combines the high-altitude lagoons with the salt flats; longer journeys also visit them but arrange the sequence differently. Choose according to the full itinerary and where your trip begins.

### Are flamingo sightings guaranteed?

No. The lagoons are known as flamingo habitats, but the presence of birds on a particular shore depends on natural conditions. Watching them is an opportunity, not a guaranteed animal encounter.

### Do I need to devote an entire day just to Hedionda?

In current Ada Tours programs, the lagoon is one of **several consecutive stops** alongside other lakes. Spending longer beside the water requires a separately agreed itinerary; published programs do not promise a full independent day on its shores.

## Laguna Honda in Bolivia: what to see

Laguna Honda lies in southwestern [Bolivia](/bolivia/), amid the high-altitude plains, salt flats and mountain ranges of the Lipez region. It is a small lake included on road routes through the chain of Andean lagoons.

Honda is distinguished by its wide-open spaces and pale water against dry, almost treeless mountains. In calm weather the surface reflects the sky; when the wind rises, the color of the water and the visibility of the shoreline change. A visit usually provides an opportunity to get out of the vehicle briefly, view the lagoon from an accessible point and compare it with nearby lakes.

For travelers, the contrast itself is compelling: water persists amid a cold, arid landscape, and birds use such places to feed. However, neither the proximity of birds nor the color of the water or condition of the shores can be guaranteed from a photograph.

## How Honda differs from the Canapa and Hedionda lagoons

On itineraries through southwestern Bolivia, Honda, [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) and [Canapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/) often form a series of stops. Each lagoon is a separate lake with its own shores and observation conditions. They can be conveniently compared while traveling the route.

[Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) is particularly well known for flamingos and mineral-rich shallows. [Canapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/) is also part of this high-altitude lake district. Honda adds a quieter panoramic experience: the shape of the shore, clarity of the air and colors of the dry slopes are especially noticeable.

The expression "Bolivian lagoons" is sometimes applied to several places at once in travel itineraries. Before setting off, check the name of each lake and the actual stops. Mentioning one lagoon in an itinerary does not mean all its neighbors will be visited.

## Where the water in high-altitude lagoons comes from

Water accumulates in high-altitude depressions through local precipitation, runoff from surrounding slopes and groundwater. Evaporation is significant in arid areas, which is why many lakes contain noticeable concentrations of dissolved minerals.

Their appearance depends on water level, bottom sediments, light and wind. Rainfall changes the shoreline and moisture in the soil. In some months, larger stretches of exposed mineral shore appear around the lakes. This is a natural process and does not necessarily mean the lake has dried up or disappeared.

The lagoons are important habitats for birds and other organisms adapted to harsh conditions. Flamingos may be seen in the area, although species and numbers vary. To observe them responsibly, use binoculars and stay at permitted viewpoints along the shore.

## How Laguna Honda fits the Lipez itinerary

On Ada Tours journeys, Laguna Honda is visited during a drive through Lipez toward the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/). Other high-altitude lakes, Canapa and Hedionda, lie along the way. It is part of a longer road trip through Bolivia's natural areas, where the sequence and duration of stops matter.

Trips through the southwest are often combined with [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) or the [Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). These places may, however, be spread across different days. Visiting them together depends on the trip's duration and actual itinerary.

Long distances at altitude are the main characteristic of this type of journey. Compare driving times, stops at the lakes and planned overnight stays. If birdwatching is your priority, ask about stops where you can safely spend more time rather than merely taking a few photographs through the window.

## What to consider at altitude

The region's lakes lie at elevations of around four thousand meters and above. Whatever the season, cold winds, intense sunshine and rapidly changing weather are possible. Warm layers and protection for your face against the wind will be useful, even for a brief stop on an exposed shore.

Altitude can affect breathing and well-being, especially for travelers who have not acclimatized. Plan your trip around a gradual ascent, rest time and individual health needs. The lakes' remoteness calls for reliable transport, drinking water and a well-planned route.

Swimming and independent water activities are not part of the usual visitor experience here. Shore deposits can be soft and unstable; avoid leaving an agreed trail or approaching feeding birds too closely.

## When to go and what to photograph

In clear weather, the lines of Honda's shoreline and the mountains on the horizon are especially striking. Morning or late-afternoon light may make the colors of the minerals and water more pronounced, although the actual stopping time depends on the route.

During the rainy season, road and shore conditions can deteriorate, while wind feels stronger in the dry, cold months. It is more useful to find out whether proper stops are planned and how long drives are organized than to seek a single "perfect" month based on Bolivia's general climate.

To compare itineraries, browse [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/) and [wildlife and nature journeys](/interests/wildlife/). Different trips allow different amounts of time at individual lagoons.

## Frequently asked questions about Laguna Honda

### Where is Laguna Honda?

In southwestern Bolivia, in the high-altitude Lipez region. It is visited on road itineraries between the highland lagoons and the Siloli Desert.

### Can I see flamingos here?

Flamingos and other high-altitude birds inhabit this area. Whether they are present at a particular shore on a particular day depends on the season and natural conditions.

### How does Honda differ from Hedionda?

They are different lakes. [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) is known for birdwatching around mineral shallows; Honda stands out for its panoramic scenery, water and dry mountains.

### Can I visit Honda together with Uyuni?

Yes, this combination appears in multi-day itineraries. Check the exact set of lakes against your chosen program.

## Laguna Honda: an optional trip among Bolivia's high-altitude lakes

[Laguna Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/) lies in southwestern Bolivia, in the Lipez region. Low shores, pale mineral bands beside the water and dry mountain slopes create the Altiplano's characteristic scenery. The lake is situated along the road to the Siloli Desert and other natural attractions of the southern highlands.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} offering Honda as an **optional** visit. It is worth considering alongside Canapa and [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), which lie on the same chain of high-altitude drives. When choosing a trip, check how much time is actually allowed at the lakes.

## An extension to a VIP journey through Peru and Bolivia

The main Bolivian section of the [18-day "Machu Picchu, the Amazon and the Uyuni Salt Flats" program](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/) introduces the salt flats and surrounding area. Separately, an Altiplano jeep day is available: lagoons [Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), Canapa, Hedionda, Chiar Khota and Honda, followed by the Ollagüe Volcano area and the Chiguana Salt Flat.

Transport, timing and the actual feasibility of this extension must be agreed in advance. The VIP itinerary already has a busy schedule with an Amazon cruise, the Andes and Machu Picchu. The additional excursion to Honda takes time beyond the main sequence, so it is not automatically included in the price and must not interfere with scheduled flights.

If you want to see several lakes in succession, choose a route where the entire high-altitude section is planned from the outset. On the [3-day Uyuni jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), Honda, Hedionda and Canapa form part of the main itinerary on day 2. This is a different kind of trip, in which remote roads and volcanic landscapes make up much of the journey.

## What makes Laguna Honda interesting along the route

Honda's appeal lies in its combination of natural details: shallow water, mineral deposits, little tall vegetation and open plateaus. In clear weather, the mountains reflect in the water; wind makes the surface choppier. Water colors vary with the light and weather.

The region is also visited for Andean flamingos, which can be observed at suitable lakes. However, birds gathering at neighboring Hedionda or Colorada do not guarantee an equally large group at Honda on the same day. Enjoy nature without expecting an identical picture-postcard scene at each lake.

The spelling "Laguna Onda" sometimes appears in Russian place names. It refers to the same Laguna Honda; there is no need to look for a separate excursion under that name.

## How to combine Honda with other stops

| Stop | Reason to visit |
|---|---|
| [Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/) | Lake and open plateau |
| [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) | Birdwatching |
| [Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) | Reddish lagoon |
| [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) | Salt flat |

In practice, many visitors first see the white expanse of Uyuni and then travel along a chain of high-altitude lagoons. These places have different natural conditions, so adequate driving time and fuel reserves are essential. A long list of lagoons cannot simply be added to a short trip without changing the entire logistics.

## Preparing for the trip

Honda is in a remote high-altitude area. The road can bring sharp temperature changes and strong sunshine despite cool air. Bring warm clothing, comfortable shoes, sunscreen and enough drinking water. Plan the excursion with acclimatization and participants' general health in mind.

Before departure, confirm that an experienced driver, suitable vehicle and agreed return time are in place. Bad weather may change access to some stops. Do not leave litter or disturb birds while observing them; conservation rules protect the entire high-altitude lake ecosystem.

A broader choice of itineraries is available in the [Bolivia tours catalog](/bolivia/tour/) and the [wildlife and nature](/interests/wildlife/) section.

## Frequently asked questions about Laguna Honda

### Where is Laguna Honda?

In southwestern Bolivia's high-altitude Lipez region, on routes between the chain of lagoons and the Siloli Desert.

### Are Honda and Onda the same place?

Yes. "Laguna Onda" is an alternative Russian rendering of the geographical name Laguna Honda.

### Is Honda included in the 18-day VIP tour?

It is mentioned on a separate optional Altiplano day. The decision to add that day and the included services are agreed for the chosen itinerary.

### Can I visit Honda and Hedionda on the same journey?

Yes. They are visited in succession on the [3-day jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/) and also appear on the optional high-altitude day in the longer VIP program.

## Which tours include Laguna Honda?

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that pass through [Laguna Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/) in Bolivia. Russian-language itineraries may also call it **"Laguna Onda"**; this is a variant of the same lake's name, not a different attraction.

Honda lies on road routes across the southwestern Altiplano, where the road connects [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), Lipez's volcanic scenery, [Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/) and [Canapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/). The purpose of this page is to help you choose **a tour that visits this particular lagoon** and identify the day devoted to high-altitude stops.

Ada Tours offers several ways to include Honda in a journey.

| Itinerary | When Honda is visited |
|---|---|
| 3-day jeep tour | Day 2, chain of lagoons |
| 10-day nature tour | Day 3, Lipez and Siloli |
| 12 days in Bolivia | Day 7, after Uyuni |
| 18 days, five countries | Day 12, on the way to Uyuni |

The **[3-day Uyuni jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/)** is suitable for a short trip among salt flats, lakes, volcanoes and unusual rock formations. On **day 2**, the route visits Honda, Hedionda and Canapa. After the lagoons, travelers cross the Siloli Desert toward the Stone Tree, then continue to Ollagüe Volcano and Puerto Chuvica. The overnight stay is in a salt hotel.

The **[10-day tour of Bolivia's natural regions](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/)** reaches Honda on **day 3**. That day's group of high-altitude lakes, known as Joyas Altoandinas, is linked to the road into the Siloli Desert. Other days cover La Paz, the salt flats, the Amazon and Lake Titicaca. It is an option for exploring several natural environments within one country.

The **[12-day "Treasures of Bolivia" tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/)** includes Honda on **day 7**. In the morning, travelers explore the Uyuni Salt Flats, Colchani and Incahuasi Island. The road then leads into Lipez, past volcanoes to the Canapa, Hedionda and Honda lagoons. Dinner and an overnight stay at Los Flamencos are included that day. Other days feature historic cities, Samaipata, Sucre and Potosí.

The **[18-day journey through five Latin American countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/)** passes Honda on **day 12**, after the Chilean Atacama section and the first part of the Bolivian jeep route. After breakfast, travelers visit the chain of lakes, then continue to Ollagüe Volcano, the Chiguana Salt Flat and Uyuni. This trip suits those who want to see several countries on a continuous itinerary.

In each of these options, Honda is on the **main route**, rather than an optional add-on. That does not mean the program devotes a whole day to the lagoon: time by the water is shared with other stops and road travel.

## How Laguna Honda differs from nearby lakes

Traveling through Lipez, visitors see several high-altitude lakes in succession. Their names can easily be confused, and photographs may make them appear to be one place. The distinctions matter when planning a route.

**[Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/)** is an open lagoon with mineral shores among dry mountain slopes. A stop here naturally combines opportunities to observe waterbirds and photograph the scenery.

**[Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/)** is known for flamingo-watching sites. Russian-language names include "Edionda" and "Edyonda." Birdwatching may be a particular focus of this stop, although both lagoons form part of the same drive on short tours.

**[Canapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/)** is another lake in the chain. It often comes before or after Honda and Hedionda in itineraries, depending on the direction of travel.

**[Chiar Khota](/bolivia/place/laguna-chiar-khota-potosi/)** does not appear in every option listed. That illustrates why the general phrase "Bolivian lagoons tour" cannot determine exactly which stops are included.

[​​Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) stands apart with its recognizable reddish water and birds along the shore. Some programs visit it the following day alongside the region's geothermal attractions. Honda's presence in a tour does not automatically confirm the other stops: always consult **the itinerary of the specific tour**.

The combination of lakes makes southwestern Bolivia so interesting because of its diversity: open shallow water edged with pale salt, birds on a lake, volcanic slopes and rocky expanses. Each lake has its own page, making it easy to compare them before choosing a journey.

## How the visit changes with the direction of travel

In the highlands, the total trip length is not the only consideration. The same group of lagoons can be crossed **on the way toward Uyuni** or **from Uyuni toward the Siloli Desert and the Chilean border**.

On the [3-day tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), the trip starts at Hito Cajones on the Chile–Bolivia border. On day 1, travelers see Laguna Verde, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geothermal area and Colorada. **Honda comes on the following day, day 2**, before the drive toward the Stone Tree and farther north. The itinerary concludes on day 3 with a visit to the Uyuni Salt Flats.

The [12-day trip](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) takes a different approach to the highlands. Day 7 begins at Uyuni, includes salt processing in Colchani and Incahuasi Island, then continues to the lakes of Lipez. This makes for a particularly full day combining salt flats and lagoons. The following day heads toward the Siloli Desert, Laguna Colorada, the geysers and Laguna Verde.

On the [18-day multi-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), Honda is visited while returning from the southern lagoons to Uyuni. **Day 12** lists Honda, Chiar Khota, Hedionda and Canapa, followed by Ollagüe, Chiguana, Colchani and Incahuasi. A packed lunch is included that day.

This comparison is more useful than an abstract promise of the "best lagoons": it shows **where you are traveling from, what you see before and after Honda, and how full the day will be**. Travelers especially keen on photographing birds should discuss the time allocated to each stop instead of assuming a long walk at every lake.

## Organizing a high-altitude journey

Routes in Lipez generally use off-road vehicles. The road crosses exposed high-altitude plateaus, rocky stretches and unpaved sections. Travelers spend long periods in the vehicle, sometimes at significant elevations. Strong winds and cold weather are possible even when it is sunny.

Included services vary by product. For instance, on **[day 3 of the 10-day tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/)**, the itinerary explicitly specifies a private 4×4 vehicle, an English- and Spanish-speaking bilingual guide, admission tickets, three meals a day and an overnight stay at Hotel Tayka del Desierto. These conditions should not automatically be attributed to the shorter jeep tour or the 18-day multi-country journey.

Warm clothing, sunglasses, UV protection, drinking water and comfortable footwear will help on the road and at short stops. If you will arrive rapidly from a lower altitude, discuss acclimatization in advance. People respond differently to altitude; avoiding uphill hikes does not remove the effects of being on a high plateau.

Binoculars are helpful for watching flamingos. Avoid approaching birds or leaving permitted shore areas: keeping the flock undisturbed matters more. Some lakes and roads may be inaccessible in difficult weather, so exact stopping times and the driving sequence are confirmed during trip arrangements.

## Choosing between a short jeep tour and a longer program

**Choose 3 days** if your main interests are the Uyuni Salt Flats, volcanoes and lagoons in a compact itinerary and you have already planned the rest of South America separately. This option has more consecutive nature stops and less variety in city visits.

**Choose 10–12 days** if you want to explore Bolivia itself. The [10-day itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/) combines the highlands with the Amazon and Lake Titicaca, while the [12-day itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) devotes time to historic cities and Samaipata. Both include Honda, but experiences beyond the lagoons differ.

**Choose a multi-country route** if you want to connect Bolivia, Chile, Peru and other countries on a single journey. The [18-day program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) includes several natural and city-based sections, leaving only part of a day for each individual lake.

For travelers interested in [flamingo watching and other nature tours of Bolivia](/interests/wildlife/tours/bolivia/), it helps to compare not only duration but also the number of stops at bird habitats, the amount of driving and the locations of overnight stays. The [Laguna Honda page](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/) describes the natural attraction itself; this page brings together tours that actually pass through it.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Laguna Onda and Laguna Honda the same place?

Yes. Russian-language programs use both **"Onda" and "Honda"**, corresponding to the Spanish name **Laguna Honda**. The Ada Tours catalog has one destination page and one set of associated itineraries for it.

### On which day of the jeep tour is Honda visited?

On the [3-day jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), the lake is included on **day 2** alongside Hedionda and Canapa. Day 3 focuses on the Uyuni Salt Flats.

### Is flamingo watching part of the itinerary?

These itineraries cross a lagoon region inhabited by flamingos. Birdwatching is a natural opportunity, but the number of birds, their proximity and photography conditions cannot be guaranteed.

### Is a separate hike to Honda required?

On the programs listed, the lagoon is visited as a stop on an **Altiplano road journey**. A separate long trek at Honda is not listed as a required activity.

### How does the 12-day tour differ from the 10-day tour?

After the lagoons, the [10-day itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/) includes the Amazon and Lake Titicaca. The [12-day itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) explores historic cities, Samaipata, Sucre and Potosí in greater depth. Both include Laguna Honda.
